findings.summary: The secret store vs CI variable comparison table lists "Rotation | none" and "Audit | none" for CI variables, which is stated more absolutely than the prose, and "Lifetime" is not a comparable axis to the prose bullets.
findings.evidence:
Rotation | none | automatic
Audit | none | full log
findings.fix: Use "manual" for CI variable rotation and "limited" for audit, matching how page 2 describes static keys as manually rotated.

findings.summary: The 'Never leak' list ends with a bullet that holds two ideas (trusting masking and how it is bypassed) and then repeats the same point in a callout.
findings.evidence:
Trust masking: base64 or split values bypass it
Masking is not protection
Masking matches the exact string only. A transformed value prints in clear.
findings.fix: Keep one statement of the masking limit: drop the 'Trust masking' bullet or the callout, and put the bypass detail in only one place.

findings.summary: The 'Never leak' list gives no reason or safe alternative for each item, and 'Pass it in command-line args' is not explained.
findings.fix: Add a short reason per item (for example: args show in process lists and logs) or the safe alternative (env var or file).

findings.summary: The AWS example shows the YAML block before the page states what the workflow must do, and the one-line takeaway follows only after the code.
findings.evidence:
yaml
permissions: {id-token: write}
...
environment: prod makes sub match; pin by SHA, not a tag
findings.fix: State the idea first (job needs id-token: write and an environment so sub matches the trust policy), then show the code.

findings.summary: The 'Mistake' section is a prose paragraph that packs two separate mistakes (wildcard repo and missing sub/aud check) into one block.
findings.evidence: repo:org/* lets any repo and any branch in the org assume the role. No sub or aud check lets any repo on GitHub in. Pin repo plus branch or environment.
findings.fix: Split into bullets: 'repo:org/* -> any repo and branch in the org'; 'no sub/aud check -> any repo on GitHub'; 'Fix: pin repo plus branch or environment'.

findings.summary: The least-privilege YAML is shown right after two bullets but the page never states in a line why a job-level write scope matters, and the 'Mistakes' public-repo item is a prose sentence under a heading-like label.
findings.evidence:
Public repo
A self-hosted runner on a public repo means any fork PR runs code on your machine
findings.fix: Make it a one-line bullet: 'Self-hosted runner on a public repo: fork PRs run code on your machine'.

findings.summary: Several bullets hold more than one idea, and the bash block mixes sign/verify commands before the flow diagram that explains them.
findings.evidence:
Keyless cosign signing uses an OIDC identity; signature goes to the Rekor log
syft lists, grype finds vulnerable versions, verify before deploy
findings.fix: Split each into separate bullets (keyless signing uses OIDC; signature is logged in Rekor; syft lists; grype finds vulnerable versions; verify before deploy) and put the flow diagram before the commands.

findings.summary: The three-proofs table has a blank header cell and the Risks bullets cram three attack types into one line without saying what each means.
findings.evidence: Risks: compromised dependency, typosquatting, dependency confusion
findings.fix: Label the table header (Artifact | Answers) and give each risk its own short bullet or a two-column risk/defence table.

findings.summary: The comparison table of pull_request vs pull_request_target has a blank first header cell, and the pwn-request bullet packs a trigger, a checkout and an outcome into one line.
findings.evidence:
Pwn request: pull_request_target + actions/checkout of PR head + running its code
Attacker gets your secrets and write token
findings.fix: Label the first header cell ('Property') and split into a short 3-step list of the ingredients plus one result line.

findings.summary: The script-injection code is shown before the page states the rule, and the rule appears afterward under a stray label.
findings.evidence:
yaml
# bad: title pasted into the script
...
Untrusted fields
Never put PR titles or branch names directly in run:.
findings.fix: Lead with the one-line rule (untrusted fields go through env:, never inline in run:), then show the bad/good code.

findings.summary: The cheat sheet's Hardening section mixes a YAML block, loose bullets and a table, and the first column of the OIDC list is not tied to any single control.
findings.evidence:
read-only by default, widen per job
Ephemeral runners
Protected branches: reviews, checks, no force push
findings.fix: Put the table first as the scannable summary and group the runner and branch bullets under it, or drop the YAML already shown on page 3.
